13 An empty cart is moving along a horizontal track at a constant velocity.
Resistive forces acting on the cart are negligible.
A heavy rock is dropped vertically into the cart.
velocity of rock
velocity
of cart
The cart continues to move horizontally with the rock inside.
How does the momentum and kinetic energy of the cart with the rock inside compare with the
momentum and kinetic energy of the empty cart?
A
The cart with the rock inside has a smaller momentum and a smaller kinetic energy.
B
The cart with the rock inside has a smaller momentum and the same kinetic energy.
C
The cart with the rock inside has the same momentum and a smaller kinetic energy.
D
The cart with the rock inside has the same momentum and the same kinetic energy.

hints: Notice the rock is dropped vertically, so its initial horizontal velocity and horizontal momentum are zero while the cart has horizontal momentum.
Recall that with negligible resistive forces there is no external horizontal force, so total horizontal momentum before and after the rock lands must be equal.
Use $E_k = p^2/(2m)$ for the horizontal motion to compare kinetic energy when $p$ is fixed but the moving mass of cart plus rock is larger.
walkthrough: Identify the horizontal system: empty cart of mass $m_c$ at velocity $v$ has momentum $p = m_c v$, while the vertically dropped rock has zero horizontal momentum.
State the conservation rule: with negligible resistive forces there is no resultant external horizontal force, so total horizontal momentum is conserved when the rock joins the cart.
Set up conservation: $m_c v = (m_c + m_r)v'$, where $v'$ is the new common horizontal velocity of cart plus rock.
Explain the velocity change: because total mass increases to $m_c + m_r$, the velocity $v'$ must be smaller than $v$ to keep $p$ the same.
Compare kinetic energy using $E_k = p^2/(2m)$: $p$ is the same but $m$ is larger, so $E_k$ after is smaller; energy is lost in the inelastic acceleration of the rock to $v'$.
Therefore momentum is the same and kinetic energy is smaller. This is option C

A.explanation: Horizontal momentum is not lost because there is no external horizontal force and the rock has zero initial horizontal momentum.

B.explanation: Momentum is conserved horizontally, and kinetic energy cannot stay the same when the cart slows down in this inelastic addition of mass.

C.explanation: Horizontal momentum is conserved so $p$ is unchanged, but $E_k = p^2/(2m)$ decreases because total moving mass $m$ increases.

D.explanation: Momentum is unchanged, but kinetic energy decreases because the rock must be accelerated horizontally by the cart in an inelastic process.
